what: Small 0.1 Bootstrap-final (Δ=0.0167) condition-identity 2x2 decomposition: sector-only shuffle vs size-percentile-only shuffle, plus a sector-gain / size-gain dose-response sweep. This is the missing low-Δ reference point for the Base-vs-Small identity argument.
harness: offline forward only (teacher-forced), same 2000-window val loader as user281434/kronos-base-cond-sector-gain-sweep and the Small C2 2x2 kernel; bare add, no γ, no training

protocol.shuffle: torch.roll(shifts=1) on the val batch; shift=2 as permutation null

checkpoint.recipe: Small 0.1 Bootstrap (chunks 1c -> 2 -> 3 -> final, all luckfu/wynstonliu), bare add, no gamma

state.delta_match: matches the preregistered target Δ=0.0167 for cum 516 / 10.3M windows to within 0.1%

judging_floor.rule: floor = max(3*|null|, retest_diff) per protocol §2 (2026-10-27 amendment)
judging_floor.rationale: Base retest of the same both-shuffled quantity differed by 2.7e-5, i.e. 15x the permutation null; permutation null alone covers only permutation noise, not reproduction noise. Same floor applied to Small for comparability.

preregistered_verdict.branch_A: if fs_sector is already order -2e-4 -> Base lags for a structural reason; gamma / injection-site work is justified
preregistered_verdict.branch_B: if fs_sector is only noise (<=3e-5) -> Base is on the normal track; close the argument
preregistered_verdict.statement: At Δ=0.0167 (the earliest measurable Small point) fs_sector is -9.2e-6, i.e. 3.3x BELOW the 3e-5 floor and well inside noise. Small at this Δ has no measurable sector identity either. Therefore Base's fs_sector (+1.2e-5 at Δ=0.0084) is NOT anomalous — it is what the same curve looks like at half the displacement.
preregistered_verdict.consequence: Close the Base-vs-Small identity dispute. Do not move gamma / injection site on the basis of Base lagging. Return to the budget arithmetic (protocol §4.2): Base reaches Small's Bootstrap-final Δ (0.0167) in ~520 more segments and Small's C2 Δ (0.0749) in ~2,325.

superlinearity_note.observation: identity effect is strongly superlinear in Δ, not proportional
superlinearity_note.reading: a fixed per-window displacement rate therefore does NOT predict identity linearly; the identity channel only becomes measurable late on the curve. This is consistent with, and now directly measured for, the protocol §4.2 'same curve, different position' reading.

readings.verdict: branch_B hit: Small at Δ=0.0167 has fs_sector = -9.2e-6, inside noise (3.3x below the 3e-5 floor). Base is on the normal track; the dispute closes.
readings.size_channel: fs_size = -3.64e-5 sits just under its own 3*|null| (4.53e-5) and marginally above the global 3e-5 floor, so it too is not separable at this Δ. Unlike C2 (where size is 3x sector), here neither channel is resolved.
readings.non_additive_at_low_delta: fs_sector + fs_size = -4.56e-5 vs fs_both = -2.72e-5, residual -1.84e-5. At C2 the same residual was only -1.1e-5 on effects 100x larger, i.e. the two channels are additive. Here everything is noise, so the residual is just fp16/permutation scatter and should not be read as channel interaction.
readings.gamma_does_not_help: alpha=8 moves fs_sector only to -3.3e-5 (still at the floor) while lowering CE by 8.1e-5. Same signature as Base: at low Δ the sector vector behaves like a small bias correction, not an identity channel.
readings.why_this_settles_it: Base at Δ=0.0084 and Small at Δ=0.0167 both show |fs_sector| <= 1.2e-5, i.e. both are noise. Base is not 'suppressed'; it is earlier on a curve that stays in noise until roughly Δ>=0.03.
readings.caveat: single checkpoint, single n=2000 draw, one permutation pair; no per-window sd or ci95 in this harness (the sweep computes only batch-weighted means). No lr_at_eval because nothing was trained.
